summary: This Wikipedia-derived note covers the 1998 season of the Milwaukee Brewers, the franchise's first season as a member of the National League. The Brewers finished fifth in the NL Central with 74 wins and 88 losses, 28 games behind the Houston Astros. The note also explains that Major League Baseball added the Arizona Diamondbacks and Tampa Bay Devil Rays before 1998, and that one club was moved from the AL Central to the NL Central to keep both leagues at an even number of teams.
one_line: Overview of the Milwaukee Brewers' 1998 season, their first in the National League, and the league realignment that moved them.
key_facts: The 1998 season was the first season for the Milwaukee Brewers franchise as a member of the National League.
The Milwaukee Brewers finished fifth in the NL Central in 1998.
The Milwaukee Brewers finished the 1998 season with a record of 74 wins and 88 losses.
The Milwaukee Brewers finished 28 games behind the Houston Astros in the 1998 NL Central standings.
Before the 1998 regular season began, Major League Baseball added the Arizona Diamondbacks and Tampa Bay Devil Rays.
The addition of the Arizona Diamondbacks and Tampa Bay Devil Rays gave the American League and National League fifteen teams each.
Major League Baseball wanted both leagues to carry an even number of teams so they could continue primarily intraleague play.
To keep an even number of teams, one club was moved from the AL Central to the NL Central.
The note states that MLB officials wanted to continue primarily intraleague play in both leagues.
